content.comment_body: Hello! I'm building a small home automation system in Sweden, using a [company_name] [product_name] controller with two expansion modules for lights and security features around my house. I want to add displays in some rooms for status monitoring and control options. I noticed there is a display for [product_name] controllers called TP 177Micro Touchpanel and was wondering if there's a similar device compatible with my current setup. How would you program such a device, is it done on the display or via PC software? Also, is it possible to connect multiple displays, and where can I purchase one? Thanks, [user_name]
Currently, there isn't a separate HMI available in the present [product_name] product range. The TP177 Micro display is designed for the [version_no] controller series.

Understood! Do you have any alternative suggestions for implementing my ideas? Should I consider changing my controller series? Since this project is for personal use, my budget is limited. Any recommendations would be appreciated. Thank you very much for your support. [user_name]

Dear [user_name], You might want to use the standard KNX/EIB module for your [company_name] [product_name], which allows you to connect various compatible elements like touch panels and weather stations. The KNX/EIB standard is internationally supported by major brands (such as ABB, Theben, etc.) for home and public automation applications. More information is available at [url]. In my experience, this solution fits your requirements and intended application well. If you need help with this setup, feel free to ask. Best regards.

Hello! Thanks for your reply. So, this device is basically a hub where several modules can be added, such as a weather station to interact with the controller? Is it also possible to connect a control panel? Do you have any suggestions for suitable control panels, or schematics showing this kind of setup? [user_name]

Hi [user_name], As previously mentioned, it's currently not possible to use an external display-based HMI device with your [product_name] modules, except those with integrated displays. Alternatively, you can use a KNX/EIB extension module and connect compatible HMI devices. For more details about EIB devices and applications, refer to: Set8, Set28. Generally, you might consider switching to the [version_no] controller series, as visualization is much easier there than on the [product_name] side. Do these options meet your needs? Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are seeking straightforward and budget-friendly methods to expand a [company_name] [product_name] setup with external HMIs. The absence of dedicated display or HMI devices for this product is noted as a significant limitation. KNX/EIB modules offer a workaround that enables integration with third-party devices, though this adds complexity.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to simply add external control panels or touch displays to their [company_name] [product_name] home automation systems, similar to those available in higher-level solutions. They focus on the need for affordable, user-friendly integration.
